text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Mubarak says that if he were in the place of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, he would submit his resignation for the cause of peace.
He also assures a meeting of business and political leaders in a speech at the end of his visit to the United States that efforts will continue to keep Egypt ripe for investment.
- Mubarak conveys condolences to Netanyahu for the shooting of Israeli schoolgirls by a Jordanian soldier.

- Mubarak tells a group of political and economic officials in Chicago that Egypt is well-placed for investment and there is a great chance for investment in the country. He says that peace is necessary for development and raising the living standards of people in the Middle East.
Egypt will not retreat from its commitment to economic reforms, he says.
- Cabinet says that shop tenants can pass their leases on to an heir if the heir is engaged in the same activity.
- Cabinet dicusses report on the trip to Washington and Paris by Mubarak as well as his efforts to arrive at comprehensive Middle East peace.
- Mubarak stops in Morocco on his way back to Egypt from the United States to meet King Hassan.
- 13 are killed in Neg Hammadi shooting spree in southern Egypt.
